doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: First recordings and easier travel with Carter
summary: His first recorded solo, Armed Forces Radio dates, and better travel conditions than in the territory band.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: And you did your first recordings with Benny Carter?
Yes, that’s true. That is true, yes. I think the one with Savannah Churchill . . .
That’s your first solo on record.
. . . I think my first solo ever, on record.
I understand you even recorded for Armed Forces Radio with that band as well as for commercial release.
Yes. I can't remember any details about that, but that did happen.

Moving from a band like Snookum Russell’s which was a territory band to a band like Benny Carter’s which traveled everywhere, what kind of changes did you notice as you were going around the country? Did you find that it was more difficult to travel when you had a band that went everywhere?

Somehow the travel conditions improved somewhat. There was a level of making arrangements for the band, let’s say. We stayed in better places. The travel conditions weren’t as rigorous or as strenuous with Benny Carter. Things in general improved.
Were you still traveling primarily by bus at that time?
A lot by bus. Sometimes by train. By all modes of transportation with Benny, as I recall.
